questions.q: What does the Wireshark packet details pane show you?
options: A summary count of all packets captured so far
Only the packet's raw hex bytes, with no layer information
The selected packet broken out layer by layer, from the Ethernet frame up through the application protocol
A list of every network interface available on the computer
questions.explain: The packet details pane breaks one packet into its layers bottom-up — frame, Ethernet, IP, TCP/UDP, and the application protocol.

questions.q: What does the display filter tcp.port == 80 do in Wireshark?
options: Only works if the capture was taken on a Windows machine
Permanently deletes every packet not on port 80
Narrows the visible packet list to traffic on port 80 (HTTP) without discarding any captured packets
Blocks all port 80 traffic from being captured in the future
questions.explain: A display filter narrows what you're viewing from an existing capture — it never deletes or discards captured data.

questions.q: What does a normal, healthy TCP connection look like in a Wireshark capture?
options: A packet with no Ethernet, IP, or TCP layer information at all
A single UDP datagram with no reply expected
Thousands of SYN packets sent to random ports with no replies
A SYN packet, followed by a SYN-ACK from the other host, followed by a final ACK, completing cleanly
questions.explain: The three-way handshake — SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK — completing cleanly is exactly what healthy TCP traffic looks like in a real capture.

questions.q: What pattern in a capture most strongly suggests a port scan is happening?
options: A single completed three-way handshake followed by a large file transfer
A DNS query followed immediately by its response
A host sending exactly one HTTP request per hour
One source IP sending SYN packets to many different destination ports in rapid succession, with almost no SYN-ACK replies
questions.explain: A scanning tool checks many ports quickly; most closed or filtered ports simply never send back a SYN-ACK.

questions.q: What is the Wireshark bytes pane useful for?
options: Changing which network interface is being captured on
Viewing a packet's raw data as hex and ASCII, which can reveal plaintext content like credentials
Writing and saving new display filters
Showing only the packet count, with no payload data
questions.explain: The bytes pane shows the identical packet data in raw hex and ASCII form, which can expose readable plaintext inside the payload.
